children: Gold futures claw back some of the losses made in the wake of the 162,000 increase in August payrolls that caused short-term Treasury yields to spike and strengthened the dollar, increasing expectations for a Fed interest-rate increase this month. The market will be closely watching next week's U.S. August CPI data. "An end to the disinflationary trend seen in June and July would signal a rate hike," BankPro CEO Paolo Broccardo says in a note. But if inflation continues to slow, "this would deal a blow to the U.S. dollar and accelerate the rally in gold, Bitcoin and the S&P500." Gold for December delivery is down 1.3% in New York at $4,481.20 a troy ounce. Silver is off 1.4% at $66.74 a troy ounce. (anthony.harrup@wsj.com)
